transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-12-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Recording: on
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Sara (LumenVerse Head of Platform), Arjun (LumenVerse SRE), Priya (LumenVerse Security)

Summary (auto): quick product walkthrough focusing on multi-tenant rate controls and burst isolation.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, with diego our se. quick intro round?
00:10 Sara: hey, sara here, head of platform at lumenverse. we run a mix of internal apps and external API, lots of bursty traffic from nightly jobs.
00:18 Arjun: arjun s r e, i'll be running the benchmarks and the infra side.
00:22 Priya: priya, security lead. we'll want SOC2 papers and network diagram.
00:30 Diego: awesome. quick agenda: org/project key model, quota slicing, burst-fencing (we call it fairburst / burst fencing), console demo to show policy setup, and then Dedicated options and next steps. sound good?
00:40 Sara: yep. main goals: keep latency under 300ms p95 for interactive features, and allow internal batch jobs to burst without taking down product API. also isolation between teams.
00:50 Diego: perfect. so at a high level we recommend org keys for company-level billing and visibility, project keys for team-level quota and routing. you can map projects to model policies, priority lanes, or dedicated pools.
01:05 Maya: just to be clear, org key gives you a single billing head and admin controls, project keys allow you to set per-team quotas and rate limits, and they can be pinned to different models or capacity tiers.
01:20 Arjun: how does burst behaviour work? we have some jobs that spike very high for short windows.
01:27 Diego: we have a couple of levers: burst-fencing (we'll also call it "fairburst" in the console) which gives a temporary high-burst allowance while smoothing sustained rate; and a leaky-bucket backpressure which protects low-latency lanes. you can set burst window, refill rate, and sticky routing to dedicated pools if you exceed thresholds.
01:46 Priya: does that affect billing or is burst capacity separate?
01:51 Maya: bursts count against usage but you can configure burst-credit policies or reserve dedicated capacity for predictable billing. for Dedicated customers we can set committed concurrency and burst lanes.
02:00 Sara: competitor question: how is this different than doing it ourselves with nginx rate limiting or a proxy?
02:06 Diego: two main things — first, model-aware routing and kv-cache aware batching. the runtime knows model kv cache behavior and will route to quantized variants automatically; second, visibility. console shows token-level cost, latency by route, and per-key tracing so you can tune policies with data, not guesswork.
02:24 Arjun: can we see the console demo?
02:28 Diego: sure, sharing screen — heading to the Console > Traffic Policies.
02:33 (screen share noise)
02:37 Diego: here we have an org level policy, and below it project policies. i'll create a new policy "internal-batch-burst" and show burst window 5m, burst multiplier 4x, refill rate 200r/s, and a sticky route to the dedicated pool named lv-dedicated-1.
03:05 Sara: that UI looks familiar, will these settings be API-configurable?
03:09 Diego: yes, every console action has a matching REST API. we show the JSON patch and you can import it into infra as code.
03:16 Maya: note also you can set soft vs hard limits — soft will queue and shed gracefully, hard will reject.
03:24 Arjun: what about priority lanes? we have external customers who must have priority over internal analytics.
03:29 Diego: you can define route priorities and assign projects to a lane. lanes map to scheduling priority in the runtime; high-priority lanes get preemptive tokens when under contention.
03:41 Sara: any gotchas with kv cache or long context windows and batching?
03:46 Diego: yes, if you have long context, batching efficiency drops and latency increases. we recommend model variants tuned for long context or using prefix caching. the console shows the sequence length distribution per route so you can tune model selection or quantization accordingly. sometimes the transcription here notes K-V cach as k v cah which is fine.
04:05 (brief cross talk)
04:12 Priya: security — can we get audit logs and per-key access controls?
04:16 Maya: yes, RBAC at org/project level, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs for all policy changes and key usage, and optional HSM/KMS key wrap for dedicated. we'll attach the SOC2 doc and a network diagram.
04:29 Priya: and for private deployment? we have some air-gapped teams...
04:33 Diego: Private deployment is supported — we provide a private control plane and on-prem runtime; for air-gapped we do an on-prem bundle. latency characteristics depend on your hardware (we'll provide recommended GPU profiles).
04:47 Arjun: can we test latency with our sample workload?
04:50 Diego: absolutely. we'll run a benchmark on Dedicated pool you saw — we'll stage the same model and run the load script. Maya, we'll follow up to schedule.
04:59 Sara: question about error modes — if we hit capacity what happens to in-flight requests?
05:04 Diego: by policy: you can queue with timeouts, failing fast, or fallback to a cheaper model variant. we also support graceful degradation with structured responses and a function call to re-try later.
05:18 Maya: for billing transparency, the console has token-level cost breakdown and per-request traces so you can reconcile invoices with traffic.
05:27 Arjun: any limitations on number of project keys? we have 250+ teams.
05:31 Diego: scale is fine — we support tens of thousands of keys; there are soft best-practices around grouping projects for easier quota management.
05:40 Sara: ok let's talk about the pilot. we want a week-long Dedicated pilot with a committed baseline and a burst buffer, plus the console access. what's the typical lead time?
05:50 Maya: for Dedicated pilot we can provision a reserved pool in 3-5 business days assuming contract terms; for Private or on-prem it's longer.
05:58 Priya: we'll need a data flow diagram and a contract addendum for audit.
06:03 Maya: will send SOC2 + network diagrams today.
06:07 Diego: i'll prepare the benchmark plan and a sample load script with varying burst patterns (pulses, sawtooth, sustained) and suggested SLO targets.
06:17 Sara: can you show an example alerting/playbook on the console? we'd like to trigger runbooks when a lane is saturated.
06:23 Diego: yes — here in Observability > Alerts you can set alert thresholds on p95 latency, rejection rate, or queue depth; attach runbook links and PagerDuty.
06:34 Arjun: small nit, how do we replay traces for an incident?
06:38 Diego: every request has a trace id; you can filter by project key, model, or route and replay the prompt for offline debugging. note we keep request payload redaction rules configurable.
06:49 Priya: retention of logs for audit?
06:51 Maya: default retention 90 days, enterprise add-on to extend to 7yrs for compliance.
06:58 Sara: what's the fallback policy if a model variant fails in the middle of a canary?
07:04 Diego: automatic fallback to the last known-good variant or to a cheaper compatibility model. canary policies include automatic rollback criteria by error rate or quality regression.
07:17 (small pause)
07:23 Maya: quick recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2/network diagram; Diego will deliver benchmark plan; we'll schedule a 1-hour perf run with Arjun; next meeting early next week to review pilot results.
07:37 Sara: sounds good.
07:41 Priya: thanks everyone.
07:44 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the console recording. bye.

Auto action items (from transcript): Maya - send docs; Diego - benchmark plan; Priya - compliance Qs.

End of transcript.
